title: Replace a worn pulley and refit its long and short screws from memory
instruction: Replace this worn timing pulley with the new one: lift out its four screws and hang them in the rack, put the worn pulley on its mat, set the new pulley on the two pins, then drop each screw back into the hole it came from, and move both arms away.
context: This task tests memory. Long and short screws have identical heads, so a screw's length shows only once it is lifted out, and then while it hangs in the open rack. Nothing in view shows which hole is deep, so the arms must remember which hole gave which length. Mixed fastener lengths are routine in robot service, and repair guides tell technicians to note which screw came from which hole, because a long screw in a short hole can do damage.
setup: Station table (wood); cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left; heights above the table. Two YAM arms, bases at y +30.5 and -30.5, start in the ready pose with the grippers open. Bench stand: machined aluminium block 17 x 17 x 4 tall, fixed, centred at x 21, y 0, with two fixed steel pins (0.4 across, 0.8 tall, tapered) at x 21, y +6.8 and -6.8. Worn pulley: the base timing pulley of a BCN3D Moveo robot arm, 16 across and 2.55 thick, printed PLA, 405 g, with belt teeth, four windows, a 3.2 hub and six 0.43 holes on a 6.8 radius; faded, with some teeth flattened; it sits on the stand over the pins, axis at x 21, y 0. New pulley: the same part, clean dark blue, on the right mat. Two mats: grey rubber discs 20 across and 0.3 thick, fixed, at x 22, y +27 (for the worn pulley) and y -27 (holding the new one). Four M4 screws with black-oxide steel shanks and identical brass-coloured knurled heads (1.4 across, 0.8 tall), standing in the worn pulley at x 24 and 18, y +6.1 and -6.1: two are long (6 under the head, 16 g), in the far-left (x 24, y +6.1) and near-right (x 18, y -6.1) holes, and two are short (3 under the head, 13 g), in the other two. The stand's holes under the long screws are 3.65 deep and those under the short screws are 0.65 deep; the deep and shallow holes look the same from above, each a black dot 0.43 across. Rack: an open machined aluminium comb, fixed, at x 32: a plate 3 x 27 x 0.6 with its top at 7, on two legs at its ends, with four slots 1 wide, open towards the robot, at y +11, +5, -5 and -11. A screw hangs in a slot by its head, its shank in plain view below.
scoring: Scored at the end of the run, or once full score has held for 1 s. Terms: a screw is long (6 cm) or short (3 cm), and the two of each length are interchangeable. A hole is deep or shallow, as in the setup. The new pulley is seated when its axis is within 5 mm of the stand's centre, its underside within 3 mm of the stand's top, and it lies within 5 degrees of flat. The worn pulley is on its mat when its axis is within 5 cm of the mat's centre, its underside is within 1 cm of the mat's top, and it moves slower than 1 cm/s. A screw is seated in a hole when its shank is within 4 mm of the hole's axis, it stands within 10 degrees of upright, and the underside of its head is within 3 mm of the pulley's top. A screw has hung in the rack once, at some moment, its shank has been within 6 mm of a slot's axis, it has stood within 10 degrees of upright, the underside of its head has been within 3 mm of the rack's top, and no gripper's fingertip has been within 3 cm of it. A hole is right when the new pulley is seated, a long screw is seated in a deep hole or a short screw in a shallow hole, that screw has hung in the rack, and no gripper's fingertip is within 3 cm of it. A long screw cannot seat in a shallow hole: it stands 2.8 cm proud. A short screw seats in a deep hole and is still wrong. If at any moment a long screw's tip comes within 2 mm of a shallow hole's floor, held or not, that hole cannot be right for the rest of the run, even after the screw is lifted out. Points: 0.1 for the worn pulley on its mat, 0.1 for the new pulley seated, 0.2 for each right hole. A total of 1.0 also needs both grippers' fingertips at least 5 cm from the pulleys and screws and every pulley and screw moving slower than 1 cm/s, all held for 1 s; without that hold it scores 0.9. Every other outcome scores what it adds up to, including 0. If the model refuses at any point, the trial ends there and scores as at the end of a run, so never 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift out the screws. Put the worn pulley back on the stand over the pins and the new one on the right mat. Stand each screw in the worn pulley, the long ones in the far-left and near-right holes.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid parts only. Screws lift out and drop in with no turning or thread. The stand, screws, rack, mats and hole depths are ours; the pulley's mesh, scale and hole positions are the real part's. A pulley hole shows 4.3 mm across but collides as an octagon 7 mm across flats, so a 4 mm shank has 1.5 mm of play. A screw's shank collides as a smooth tapered rod. Physics runs at 240 Hz on GPU PhysX. The two fingers are independent joints.
